git diff 0397dec -- idiomatic-elixir/ touches SKILL.md (the When to load and Reviewing code bullets, a defstruct sentence in Update structs, two new rules (Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call; Open a module with `use`, `import`, `alias`, `require`, in that order), the do: rule and step 4 of Before you finish), references/processes.md and references/testing.md. macros.md and library-design.md are unchanged, so the seven macro and library rules are graded to the standard of sweeps/2026-10-22-b/grades/macro-dsl-skill.json: a direct attribute write inside get's quote counts against Keep quote blocks small, validation in the macro body outside quote does not; the use documentation rule needs an admonition at the top of @moduledoc; __using__ and __before_compile__ without @doc false are accepted because their __ names hide them (Code.fetch_docs reports :hidden for every __ function and macro in all five runs); `if not ... raise` validation is not counted under the branching rule; a one-line multi-step pipeline is listed under the pipeline rule; String.to_atom on route text from source code (haiku-1 line 71, haiku-2 line 93) is not counted under the atom rule; a format failure whose only change is parentheses on the two get calls is recorded as ok apart from locals_without_parens.

Changed rule, graded against its current text in idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md (Readability), sentence by sentence as in sweeps/2026-10-22-check-6/grades/macro-dsl-skill.json: Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else. Since 0397dec its wrapped-line sentence was rewritten to "A `do:` body belongs on the head's line: when `mix format` moves it onto a line of its own, the body is too long for `do:`, so write a block or move part of the body into a helper. The one wrap to keep is a head that `mix format` breaks after a long guard, with `do:` on the next line.", and the sentence "The same holds for `if`: `if ..., do: ..., else: ...` fits when each branch is one short expression on the `if`'s line, and a branch `mix format` moves onto its own line gets `do ... end`." was added. Neither changed sentence decides a violation in this sweep; both violations are decided by the unchanged sentence "When most of a function's clauses need blocks, write all of them as blocks.", and the guard sentence decides that sonnet-1's one wrapped do: line is kept.

do: rule, violating runs out of five, per sentence. "Use `do:` for a body of one expression that reads as part of the head": 0 of 5 (every do: body is one call, a literal or a match?). Two judgement calls that decide no verdict, as at check-3: sonnet-2's generated match/1 (lines 81-83) is a block whose do: form, `def match(path) when is_binary(path), do: match_segments(TinyRouter.split(path))`, fits at 86 characters inside the quote; opus-1's `if not module_name?(handler) do` / `raise_invalid_handler!(handler)` / `end` (lines 115-117) would fit as `if ..., do:` at 69 characters, which the if sentence allows but does not require. "A body with several steps, a `case` or `with`, or a comment gets `do ... end`.": 0 of 5. "A function whose clauses are short pattern matches keeps them on `do:` even when one clause needs a block; set that clause apart with a blank line.": 0 of 5; every mixed function sets its block clauses apart. "When most of a function's clauses need blocks, write all of them as blocks.": 2 of 5. opus-1 validate_path!/1 (lines 104-112) and sonnet-1 validate_path!/1 (lines 117-125) each keep `defp validate_path!("/" <> _rest), do: :ok` beside two raise block clauses whose do: forms wrap (opus-1 144 and 118 characters joined, sonnet-1 133 and 107), so two of three clauses need blocks; this is the shape 2026-10-22-b sonnet-1 and check-3's two Sonnet runs broke. sonnet-2's __define__/3 has three of three clauses needing blocks and writes all as blocks. "A `do:` body belongs on the head's line ... move part of the body into a helper.": 0 of 5. "The one wrap to keep is a head that `mix format` breaks after a long guard, with `do:` on the next line.": exercised by sonnet-1 only and kept correctly. "The same holds for `if` ...": 0 of 5; haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 write each validation if as a block whose do: form wraps (haiku-1 lines 35 and 40 at 126 and 171 characters joined, haiku-2 lines 75 and 80 at 126 and 141, sonnet-2 lines 94 and 98 at 122 and 135); sonnet-1 writes no if. Any sentence: 2 of 5 (opus-1, sonnet-1): Opus violated, Haiku clean, Sonnet violated.

Every do: body on a function or an if that mix format leaves on a line of its own, quoted: one in five files. sonnet-1 lines 127-128: `defp validate_handler!(handler) when is_atom(handler) and handler not in [nil, true, false],` / `do: :ok`. Its head has a long guard (102 characters joined, so mix format breaks after the guard), which is the one wrap the rule keeps; the transcript shows sonnet-1 wrote this shape itself in its heredoc and in its Write call, not that mix format produced it. opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 have none (grep for lines starting with do: or else: finds only sonnet-1 line 128). No if in any file is written with do:.

One-expression blocks measured: each was rewritten as a do: line at its real nesting depth and run through Code.format_string!. Segment matchers (four clauses, two short do: clauses and two recursive block clauses set apart by blank lines, in all five runs): opus-1 160 and 133 characters, haiku-1 124 and 144, haiku-2 match_pattern/3 123 and 144, sonnet-1 141 and 117; all wrap, and two of four is not most, so clean everywhere. Others that wrap: opus-1 generated match/1 (114; its guard is short, so this would not be the guard wrap) and raise_invalid_handler!/1 (172); haiku-1 generated match/1 (107); sonnet-1 validate_handler!/1 raise clause (150); sonnet-2 __define__/3 raise clauses (155 and 127) and the generated match_segments/1 clause in match_clause/1 (102). Fit as written on do:: haiku-2 line 68 `def match(path), do: TinyRouter.__match__(unquote(Macro.escape(matchers)), path)` and sonnet-1 line 77. The two blocks that would fit are the judgement calls above.

Compile-time dependencies verified with mix xref trace, one scratch Mix project per run: the run's file copied unchanged to lib/tiny_router.ex (so xref line numbers match the run file) plus real MyApp.PageHandler and MyApp.UserHandler modules in lib/handlers.ex. opus-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 (Macro.expand_literals with function {:match, 1}) and haiku-2 (with {:call, 2}, a function the router does not define, which still puts the alias in a function context) report alias MyApp.PageHandler (runtime). haiku-1 never expands the handler and passes the alias into __define__/3, which runs in the router's module body: lib/tiny_router.ex:104: alias MyApp.PageHandler (compile).

Bad-declaration checks: each run's project loaded with mix run, then Code.compile_string compiled one router declaring get 123, MyApp.PageHandler and one declaring get "/", "not a module". All ten fail with ArgumentError while the router compiles, raised from the @doc false __define__/3 that get's quote calls. All five compile under mix compile --warnings-as-errors.

Format: opus-1 passes mix format --check-formatted as written (it ran mix format and kept get("/", MyApp.PageHandler)). In the other four, mix format on a copy changes only the two get calls in MyApp.Router to parentheses, so result.json's format_ok is false for that reason alone and they are recorded as ok apart from locals_without_parens. The transcripts show the choice was deliberate: haiku-1 and haiku-2 said they left the user's paren-less example as written, and sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 ran mix format and then used Edit to put the paren-less get calls back.

Reads: all five read SKILL.md, macros.md and library-design.md before writing tiny_router.ex. haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 used one Read call per file; opus-1 and sonnet-1 read both references with one cat in a Bash call. This matches result.json reads and satisfies the Expected reads line.

Against 2026-10-22-b's skill runs: the do: rule moves from clean to violated on Opus (opus-1's validate_path!/1), from violated to clean on Haiku, and stays violated on Sonnet through the same sentence and the same function as b's sonnet-1. Keep quote blocks small moves from violated to clean on Sonnet; all five get quotes call __define__/3. The compile-time-dependency rule stays violated on Haiku (haiku-1 only; haiku-2 now uses Macro.expand_literals) and clean on Opus and Sonnet. The other five rules stay clean on every tier. Both haiku runs write the one-line three-step pipeline in __before_compile__; opus-1 and both sonnet runs split it over lines.

Smoke test outside the rules: all five return routes in declaration order, match "/", "/users/42" and "/users/42/", and return :error for "/nope". haiku-1 and haiku-2 return atom param keys (%{id: "42"}); opus-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 return string keys. sonnet-2 generates one private match_segments/1 clause per route; the other four match at runtime through a @doc false __match__/2.
